intro: Wisconsin uses two tests: a 15-question Highway Signs Test (12 correct to pass) and a 50-question Knowledge Test (40 correct to pass).

testTypes.name: Regular driver (Class D)
testTypes.description: Highway Signs Test and Knowledge Test for the Class D instruction permit.

notes: Knowledge Test: 50 questions, 40 correct (80%) to pass; takes about 45 minutes.
Highway Signs Test: 15 questions, 12 correct (80%) to pass.
Applicants ages 15–17 may take the knowledge test online for a fee.

mockPresets.label: Knowledge test mock
mockPresets.description: Official format is 50 questions with 40 correct to pass. Our verified bank is still growing, so this mock uses every available non-sign question and scores at 80%.

mockPresets.label: Highway Signs Test mock
mockPresets.description: Official format: 15 sign questions, 12 correct to pass.

commonMistakes.text: Using the two-second rule. Wisconsin teaches a four-second following distance, plus a second for each adverse condition.
commonMistakes.sourceSection: Section 3: The Basics — B. Understanding Vehicle Speed

commonMistakes.text: Stopping in the intersection on a yellow. If you are already in it when the light turns yellow, keep going.
Mixing up hill parking: uphill with a curb is wheels LEFT; uphill without a curb and downhill are wheels RIGHT.
Forgetting the school-zone limit is 15 mph when children are present, not 25.
commonMistakes.sourceSection: Section 3: The Basics — B. Understanding Vehicle Speed

faq.q: How many questions are on the Wisconsin permit test?
faq.a: There are two tests: the Highway Signs Test (15 questions, 12 correct to pass) and the Knowledge Test (50 questions, 40 correct to pass).

faq.q: Can I take the Wisconsin knowledge test online?
faq.a: Applicants between ages 15 and 17 may take the knowledge test online for a fee of $10. Tests at a DMV customer service center are free.

faq.q: How many supervised driving hours do I need?
faq.a: Drivers under 18 must complete at least 50 hours, 10 of them during darkness, verified by their sponsor.

faq.q: Are these official Wisconsin DMV questions?
faq.a: No. They are original practice questions written from the Wisconsin Motorists' Handbook. Wisconsin DMV also offers its own free practice test, linked on this page.

questions.question: How many questions are on Wisconsin's knowledge test, and how many must you answer correctly?
questions.explanation: The knowledge test includes 50 questions and you need to answer 40 (80%) correctly. It takes about 45 minutes.
questions.sourceSection: Section 1: Driving Test Requirements — C. Knowledge Test

questions.question: Wisconsin's separate Highway Signs Test has how many questions?
questions.explanation: There are 15 questions on the Highway Signs Test and you need to answer 12 (80%) correctly.
questions.sourceSection: Section 1: Driving Test Requirements — B. Highway Signs Test

questions.question: Wisconsin's vision requirement for regular car applicants includes visual acuity of at least:
options: 20/40 in one eye, plus a 70-degree field of vision from the center of each eye
questions.correctAnswer: 20/40 in one eye, plus a 70-degree field of vision from the center of each eye
questions.explanation: Applicants need visual acuity of at least 20/40 in one eye (corrected or uncorrected) and a 70-degree field of vision from the center of each eye.
questions.sourceSection: Section 1: Driving Test Requirements — A. Vision Screening

questions.question: What is the minimum age for a Wisconsin instruction permit?
questions.explanation: If under 18, you must be at least 15, pass the knowledge test, signs test and vision screening, and be enrolled in driver education including behind-the-wheel.
questions.sourceSection: Section 2: Progression of Licenses — B. Instruction Permit

questions.question: Under 18, how many hours of supervised driving must your sponsor verify before a probationary license?
questions.explanation: With a valid instruction permit you must practice at least 40 hours in daylight and 10 hours in darkness — 50 total — verified by your sponsor.
questions.sourceSection: Section 2: Progression of Licenses — C. Probationary License

questions.question: With a Wisconsin instruction permit, who must be in the seat beside you when you drive during hours of darkness?
options: A qualified instructor, or a licensed person age 25+ with at least two years of driving experience
No one — permits allow solo night driving
questions.correctAnswer: A qualified instructor, or a licensed person age 25+ with at least two years of driving experience
questions.explanation: During hours of darkness, a permit holder must be accompanied by a qualified instructor or a licensed person 25 or older with at least two years of licensed driving experience in the seat beside them.
questions.sourceSection: Section 2: Progression of Licenses — B. Instruction Permit

questions.question: For drivers under 18, Wisconsin's graduated driver license (GDL) restrictions apply for the first:
questions.explanation: GDL passenger and hour restrictions are required for the first nine months, unless you turn 18 before then. Violations can extend them six months.
questions.sourceSection: Section 2: Progression of Licenses — C. Probationary License

questions.question: When may an instruction permit or probationary license holder use a cell phone while driving in Wisconsin?
options: When a licensed adult is present
questions.explanation: Instruction permit and probationary license holders can only use a cell phone to report an emergency.
questions.sourceSection: Section 9: Dangerous Driving Behaviors — B. Distracted Driving

questions.question: What following-distance rule does the Wisconsin handbook teach?
options: The four-second rule, adding a second for each adverse condition
questions.correctAnswer: The four-second rule, adding a second for each adverse condition
questions.explanation: Use the Four Second Following Distance Rule. Add a second for every adverse condition such as heavier traffic, rain, snow or ice.
questions.sourceSection: Section 3: The Basics — B. Understanding Vehicle Speed

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in Wisconsin residential areas?
questions.explanation: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in residential areas is 25 miles per hour.
questions.sourceSection: Section 3: The Basics — B. Understanding Vehicle Speed

questions.question: What is the normal speed limit in a Wisconsin school zone when children are present?
questions.explanation: The normal speed limit in a school zone when children are present is 15 miles per hour.
questions.sourceSection: Section 3: The Basics — B. Understanding Vehicle Speed

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit in outlying parts of cities and villages with no posted speed limit?
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit in outlying parts of cities and villages with no posted speed limit is 35 mph.
questions.sourceSection: Section 3: The Basics — B. Understanding Vehicle Speed

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane. How far away should you stop?
options: At least ten feet away until the person is off the roadway
No set distance — just slow down
questions.correctAnswer: At least ten feet away until the person is off the roadway
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, even if they are not in the intersection. Stop at least ten feet away until the person is off the roadway.
questions.sourceSection: Section 3: The Basics — A. Right-Of-Way

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at a four-way stop at the same time. Who goes first?
questions.explanation: Yield to the driver who arrives first at a four-way stop. If drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.
questions.sourceSection: Section 3: The Basics — A. Right-Of-Way

questions.question: Wisconsin requires low-beam headlights when you cannot see a vehicle or person how far away?
questions.explanation: You must use low beams when you cannot see a vehicle or person 500 feet (about one block) away, and from a half hour past sunset to a half hour before sunrise.
questions.sourceSection: Section 3: The Basics — K. Communication

questions.question: When turning at an intersection, how early should you start signaling?
options: About three seconds (about 100 feet) before the turn
questions.correctAnswer: About three seconds (about 100 feet) before the turn
questions.explanation: If you are turning at an intersection, start signaling about three seconds (about 100 feet) before the turn.
questions.sourceSection: Section 3: The Basics — K. Communication

questions.question: Parking uphill next to a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: All the way to the left
All the way to the right
It doesn't matter if the brake is set
questions.correctAnswer: All the way to the left
questions.explanation: Parked uphill with a curb, turn your wheels all the way to the left. Uphill without a curb, turn them right. Downhill, turn them right. Set your parking brake.
questions.sourceSection: Section 3: The Basics — J. Parking

questions.question: Parking downhill, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: All the way to the right
All the way to the left
Left only if there is a curb
questions.correctAnswer: All the way to the right
questions.explanation: If you are parked downhill, move your wheels all the way to the right and set your emergency brake.
questions.sourceSection: Section 3: The Basics — J. Parking

questions.question: In Wisconsin, parking is not allowed:
options: On any residential street at night
Where curbs have yellow markings or in front of fire hydrants
questions.correctAnswer: Where curbs have yellow markings or in front of fire hydrants
questions.explanation: Parking is not allowed where there are yellow markings on the curb or in areas in front of fire hydrants. Also check for No Parking signs.
questions.sourceSection: Section 3: The Basics — J. Parking

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing, you must stop at least:
questions.explanation: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing, stop at least 20 feet from it, whether it is on your side of the road or the opposite side.
questions.sourceSection: Section 10: Sharing the Road — C. School Buses

questions.question: When do you NOT need to stop for a school bus flashing red lights in Wisconsin?
options: When it is on the opposite side of a two-lane road
When you are already past the bus's front bumper
When it is on the other side of a divided highway with a barrier
questions.correctAnswer: When it is on the other side of a divided highway with a barrier
questions.explanation: If you are on a divided highway and not on the side of the school bus, you do not need to stop. A divided highway has a barrier between opposing lanes.
questions.sourceSection: Section 10: Sharing the Road — C. School Buses

questions.question: When passing a bicyclist, give them at least:
options: A full lane at all times
questions.explanation: Give bicyclists at least three feet of room when you pass, and wait for oncoming traffic to clear before passing.
questions.sourceSection: Section 10: Sharing the Road — E. Bicycles

questions.question: How much room should you give a snowplow with flashing red, amber or green lights?
questions.explanation: Give snowplows at least 200 feet of room when their lights are flashing red, amber or green.
questions.sourceSection: Section 7: Driving Conditions — C. Winter

questions.question: According to the Wisconsin handbook, a large truck's No-Zone extends about:
options: 50 feet behind and 5 feet in front
200 feet behind and 20 feet in front
100 feet behind and 50 feet in front
20 feet behind and 200 feet in front
questions.correctAnswer: 200 feet behind and 20 feet in front
questions.explanation: No-Zones are areas where large vehicles cannot see you — about 200 feet behind and 20 feet in front of large trucks.
questions.sourceSection: Section 10: Sharing the Road — F. No-Zones

questions.question: What alcohol concentration is allowed for Wisconsin drivers under age 21?
questions.explanation: The legal alcohol concentration allowed for drivers under 21 is 0.00% — you cannot have any alcohol in your system while driving.
questions.sourceSection: Section 9: Dangerous Driving Behaviors — A. Alcohol, Drugs and Driving

questions.question: If you refuse an officer's request to take a prohibited alcohol concentration (PAC) test, you will lose your driving privileges for at least:
questions.explanation: Under the Implied Consent Law, if you refuse, the officer must arrest you and you will lose your driving privileges for at least one year.
questions.sourceSection: Section 9: Dangerous Driving Behaviors — A. Alcohol, Drugs and Driving (Implied Consent)

questions.question: Your Wisconsin driving privilege will be suspended or revoked if you get how many demerit points within 12 months?
questions.explanation: You will not be able to drive if you get 12 or more demerit points within any 12-month period.
questions.sourceSection: Section 11: Your Driving Privilege — A. Point System

questions.question: A crash with no injuries must still be reported to police if property damage is:
questions.explanation: Report a crash to police if there is injury or death, property damage of $1,000 or more, government property damage of $200 or more, a vehicle can't be moved, or a driver appears impaired.
questions.sourceSection: Section 8: Handling Emergencies — B. Crashes

questions.question: Your car begins to hydroplane. What should you do?
options: Ease off the gas, keep the wheel straight, and don't stop or turn until the tires grip
questions.correctAnswer: Ease off the gas, keep the wheel straight, and don't stop or turn until the tires grip
questions.explanation: If you hydroplane, ease your foot off the gas, keep the wheel straight, and do not try to stop or turn until your tires are gripping the road again.
questions.sourceSection: Section 7: Driving Conditions — B. Severe Weather

questions.question: If your brakes stop working, what is the first step the handbook lists?
options: Pump the brake pedal several times
questions.correctAnswer: Pump the brake pedal several times
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail: pump the brake pedal several times, pull the parking brake (release it if you skid), and look for a safe place to slow to a stop.
questions.sourceSection: Section 8: Handling Emergencies — C. Roadside Emergencies

questions.question: Generally, Wisconsin children must ride in a child safety seat until age ___ and a booster seat until age ___.
questions.explanation: Generally, children must be in a child safety seat until age four and in a booster seat until age eight.
questions.sourceSection: Section 12: Other Important Information — D. Seat Belts

questions.question: A red sign with eight sides and white letters means:
options: Come to a complete stop and wait until your path is clear
questions.correctAnswer: Come to a complete stop and wait until your path is clear
questions.explanation: The stop sign has eight sides and is red with white letters. You must come to a complete stop and wait until your path is clear.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — B. Regulatory

questions.question: A downward-pointing red and white triangle means:
questions.explanation: The Yield sign is a downward-pointing red and white triangle. It means you must yield the right-of-way to other vehicles.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — B. Regulatory

questions.question: A yellow pennant-shaped sign with black lettering marks:
questions.explanation: The No Passing Zone sign is a yellow pennant with black lettering. You may not pass any vehicle in the no passing zone.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — B. Regulatory

questions.question: A triangle with reflective orange markings on the back of a vehicle means the vehicle:
questions.explanation: The Slow Moving Vehicle sign is triangle-shaped with reflective orange markings; the vehicle could travel at 25 mph or less.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — B. Regulatory

questions.question: Warning signs in Wisconsin are:
options: Yellow with black lettering or symbols, and most are diamond-shaped
questions.correctAnswer: Yellow with black lettering or symbols, and most are diamond-shaped
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. Most are diamond shaped and warn of a special situation or hazard ahead.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — A. Warning

questions.question: Orange diamond or rectangle signs indicate a work zone. What else is true in these areas?
options: Cell phones may be used hands-free only
questions.explanation: Construction signs are orange with black lettering. Traffic fines double in these areas, and you can only use your cellphone to report an emergency.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — C. Construction

questions.question: Green or brown signs with white lettering are:
options: Destination signs showing directions and distances
questions.correctAnswer: Destination signs showing directions and distances
questions.explanation: Destination signs are square or rectangular, green or brown with white lettering, and show directions and distance to places. Brown signs point to recreational or scenic places.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — D. Destination

questions.question: Blue signs with white letters or symbols are:
options: Service signs, such as hospital or camping
questions.correctAnswer: Service signs, such as hospital or camping
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters or symbols and show how to get to services nearby, such as camping or a hospital.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — E. Service

questions.question: A round yellow sign with an "X" and the letters R R means:
questions.explanation: The Railroad Crossing Warning sign is round with a yellow background and an X symbol with black lettering.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — H. Railroad Crossing

questions.question: A Do Not Enter sign is commonly used:
options: At the end of construction zones
On exit ramps going the wrong direction or one-way streets
questions.correctAnswer: On exit ramps going the wrong direction or one-way streets
questions.explanation: Do Not Enter means you cannot enter. It is used on exit ramps going the wrong direction or one-way streets.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — B. Regulatory

questions.question: School crossing and school zone warning signs in Wisconsin may be:
questions.explanation: School Crossing / School Zone signs may be fluorescent green or yellow and show pedestrians with an arrow. Yield to crossing pedestrians.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — A. Warning

questions.question: What does a Keep Right sign tell you?
options: A traffic island or obstacle divides the road ahead
Passing is required on the right
questions.correctAnswer: A traffic island or obstacle divides the road ahead
questions.explanation: Keep Right means a traffic island or obstacle divides the road ahead.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — B. Regulatory

questions.question: A blue sign with white lettering at a highway-railroad crossing shows:
options: The distance to the next station
A phone number to report problems or emergencies
questions.correctAnswer: A phone number to report problems or emergencies
questions.explanation: The Report Problem or Emergency sign is blue with white lettering, posted at every highway-railroad crossing, and shows a phone number to report unsafe conditions.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — H. Railroad Crossing

questions.question: A railroad crossing gate is lowering. What should you do?
options: Stop — never drive around or under a lowering or raised gate
Drive around it if no train is visible
questions.correctAnswer: Stop — never drive around or under a lowering or raised gate
questions.explanation: Train gates lower when a train is coming. Do not drive around the gate or under a raising or lowering gate.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — H. Railroad Crossing

questions.question: The light turns steady yellow while you are already in the intersection. What should you do?
options: Back up behind the stop line
Turn right to avoid the light
questions.explanation: A steady yellow means the light is about to change to red; stop before entering the intersection. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, do not stop — continue through.
questions.sourceSection: Section 5: Signals, Pavement Markings and Lane Controls — A. Traffic Signals

questions.question: When may you turn left on a steady red light in Wisconsin?
options: When turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street, after stopping and yielding
Only with a flashing yellow arrow
questions.correctAnswer: When turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street, after stopping and yielding
questions.explanation: You may turn left on red if you are turning from a one-way onto a one-way street. Stop first, yield to all traffic, then proceed.
questions.sourceSection: Section 5: Signals, Pavement Markings and Lane Controls — A. Traffic Signals

questions.question: A solid white line between lanes means:
options: Do not cross it unless there is a hazard or you're turning within the next block
questions.correctAnswer: Do not cross it unless there is a hazard or you're turning within the next block
questions.explanation: A solid white line between lanes means you cannot cross, except for a hazard or if you are turning within the next block.
questions.sourceSection: Section 5: Signals, Pavement Markings and Lane Controls — B. Types of Line Markings

questions.question: A flashing yellow arrow means:
options: Protected turn — oncoming traffic is stopped
Yield first, then turn with caution
questions.correctAnswer: Yield first, then turn with caution
questions.explanation: Flashing Yellow Arrow: yield first before turning and proceed with caution.
questions.sourceSection: Section 5: Signals, Pavement Markings and Lane Controls — A. Traffic Signals

questions.question: How far ahead should you be able to see to keep good control of your vehicle?
questions.explanation: To have better control, you need to see 10 to 15 seconds ahead. If you cannot, slow down.
questions.sourceSection: Section 3: The Basics — E. Sight Distance Rule

questions.question: How often should you check your rearview mirror for tailgaters?
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror every 6 to 8 seconds to see if someone is following too closely.
questions.sourceSection: Section 3: The Basics — F. Space Between Vehicles

questions.question: As you enter a Wisconsin roundabout, you should:
options: Expect traffic in the roundabout to yield to you
Yield to traffic on your left that is already in the roundabout
Stop even if the roundabout is empty
questions.correctAnswer: Yield to traffic on your left that is already in the roundabout
questions.explanation: Traffic moves counterclockwise. Slow down, yield to pedestrians and bicycles, and yield to traffic on your left already in the roundabout. If it's empty, you do not need to wait.
questions.sourceSection: Section 6: Driving Situations — A. Roundabouts

questions.question: You are already inside a roundabout when an emergency vehicle with its siren on enters. What should you do?
options: Safely exit at the next right, then pull over
Speed up and circle until it passes
questions.correctAnswer: Safely exit at the next right, then pull over
questions.explanation: If you are already in the roundabout, safely exit at the next right, then pull over. Avoid stopping in the roundabout.
questions.sourceSection: Section 6: Driving Situations — A. Roundabouts

questions.question: When are deer most active, according to the Wisconsin handbook?
questions.explanation: Deer are most active in the sunset to sunrise hours. Scan for the reflection of your headlights in their eyes and watch for more than one deer.
questions.sourceSection: Section 6: Driving Situations — E. Watch for Deer

questions.question: You see a 2-Way Traffic warning sign. What does it tell you?
options: Passing is allowed in both directions
You are leaving a one-way roadway and entering a road with opposing traffic
questions.correctAnswer: You are leaving a one-way roadway and entering a road with opposing traffic
questions.explanation: The 2-Way Traffic sign appears when you are leaving a one-way roadway and entering a roadway with opposing traffic.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — A. Warning

questions.question: What should you do when you see a Reduced Speed Ahead sign?
options: Speed up to the new limit
questions.explanation: Reduced Speed Ahead means that you should slow down — for example, the road ahead may be slippery.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — B. Regulatory

questions.question: Tall, thin blue or green mile marker signs along the highway help:
options: Show the speed limit for trucks
Mark the start of a work zone
Show distance to the next rest area
Show where you are on the road and improve emergency response times
questions.correctAnswer: Show where you are on the road and improve emergency response times
questions.explanation: Mile markers (reference markers) are tall, thin rectangular blue or green signs with the direction, route and mile number. They help locate you and improve emergency response times.
questions.sourceSection: Section 4: Signs — F. Mile Marker
